rows.selection_reason: With no completed experiments, the highest-priority question is establishing a performance floor. config_007 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000, no aggregation, no fusion) is the simplest possible configuration: it requires no trained encoder (PCA is instantaneous), uses a single profile, and has no aggregation or fusion steps. This gives us a clean, fast, low-risk baseline that will serve as the reference point for every subsequent comparison—whether multiprofile helps, whether image modality adds value, whether learned encoders (scgpt, scvi) outperform PCA, and whether aggregation/fusion strategies improve performance. Starting here minimizes implementation risk, is computationally cheap, and maximizes the interpretability of all future deltas. Without this floor, we cannot determine whether any added complexity actually contributes.

We have only one completed experiment (config_007: RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA, acc≈0.485), so evidence is extremely sparse and the most critical uncertainty is whether adding the image modality provides any signal at all. config_009 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, no aggregation, concat fusion) is the minimal, clean extension of config_007: it keeps the RNA side identical (same encoder, same profile setting) and adds only a simple ResNet50 image branch with basic concatenation. This isolates the effect of image information without confounding changes to the RNA encoder, profile count, aggregation, or fusion complexity. If accuracy improves, it validates the multimodal premise and justifies investing further in image encoders and fusion strategies; if it does not, it redirects the budget toward RNA representation (scgpt/scvi) or multiprofile aggregation. Under a limited budget, resolving this core question before exploring more complex multimodal or learned-encoder configurations is the highest-information next step.

Evidence: config_007 (rna_only, pca_n2000, singleprofile) achieved 0.485 acc, and config_009 (multimodal, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat, singleprofile) improved to 0.527 acc, confirming that adding image modality helps. However, both experiments use pca_n2000—a linear dimensionality reduction—as the RNA encoder. It is unclear whether this linear representation is a bottleneck for the RNA branch in the multimodal setting. Question: config_004 (multimodal, singleprofile, scgpt, resnet50, concat) is a clean single-variable comparison to config_009, changing only the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to the learned scgpt representation. This isolates the effect of RNA representation quality while holding image encoder, fusion, and profile setting constant. Why this is the best next experiment: with only two data points, the most impactful uncertainty to resolve is whether a learned RNA encoder provides a meaningful gain over PCA in the multimodal pipeline. If scgpt substantially outperforms pca_n2000, it validates investing in learned representations and opens a high-performing branch for further exploration (multiprofile, aggregation, stronger image encoders). If the gain is marginal, it suggests the current PCA representation is sufficient and budget should shift to testing multiprofile or image encoder upgrades. This single-variable design maximizes information per experiment under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_009 (pca_n2000 + resnet50, concat, singleprofile) is the best so far at 0.527 acc, clearly outperforming both the RNA-only baseline (config_007, 0.485) and the scgpt variant (config_004, 0.427). This establishes pca_n2000 + resnet50 + concat as a strong backbone. Uncertainty: All three completed experiments use singleprofile; we have zero evidence on whether multiprofile + aggregation adds value. Question: config_010 extends the best-known configuration by moving from singleprofile to multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, while keeping the proven RNA encoder (pca_n2000), image encoder (resnet50), and fusion (concat) fixed. This isolates the effect of multiprofile aggregation as the primary new variable. Why best: It is the most natural exploitation of our strongest evidence while exploring the single largest untested design dimension (profile setting). Testing multiprofile now, before investing in further fusion or image-encoder variants, tells us whether the added complexity of multi-profile aggregation is worthwhile, which will shape all subsequent experiments.

Evidence: config_010 (pca_n2000, resnet50, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) is the strongest result so far at 0.6186 acc, and it clearly outperforms its singleprofile counterpart config_009 (0.5266), establishing multiprofile+avgpool as a key design choice. We also know pca_n2000 > scgpt for RNA (config_009 vs config_004). However, no experiment has yet tested a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) in the multiprofile setting. Question: Does upgrading the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l improve performance when all other components (pca_n2000, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) are held at their proven best? Why this is the best next experiment: config_021 changes exactly one variable (image encoder) relative to the current best config_010, cleanly isolating the effect of image representation quality. If imagenet_vit_l helps, it identifies image encoding as a further lever; if it does not, it tells us the bottleneck lies elsewhere (aggregation, fusion, RNA encoder) and we can redirect the remaining budget accordingly. This is the highest-information single-variable test available.

Evidence: The current best is config_021 (acc=0.629, F1=0.599) with multiprofile + pca_n2000 + ViT-L + avgpool + concat. The jump from singleprofile (config_009, 0.527) to multiprofile+avgpool (config_010, 0.619) was the largest gain observed, but aggregation has only been tested as avgpool. Uncertainty: It is unknown whether a more expressive aggregation (transformer) can further improve over simple average pooling when combining multiple profiles. Question tested: config_045 changes only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding all other factors constant (pca_n2000, ViT-L, multiprofile, concat), giving a clean single-variable comparison against config_021. Why this is the best next experiment: Aggregation is a fundamental design choice for how multiprofile information is combined, and the potential gain from a learned (transformer) aggregation over a fixed (avgpool) one is a major open question. Isolating this single factor on the current best configuration maximizes information per experiment and directly informs whether to invest further in transformer-based aggregation or confirm avgpool sufficiency.

Evidence: The current best (config_021: pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.629 acc / 0.599 F1. All six completed multiprofile experiments use concat fusion; weighted fusion has never been tested in the multiprofile setting. Aggregation (avgpool > transformer) and image encoder (vit_l ≥ resnet50) effects are partially characterized, but the fusion strategy remains entirely unexplored at the multiprofile level. Question: Does learned weighted fusion outperform simple concatenation when combining RNA and image representations across multiple profiles? config_002 is identical to config_021 in every dimension except fusion (weighted vs concat), making it a clean single-variable comparison. Why best under budget: It directly tests the highest-priority unexplored design axis on the current best configuration. A positive result would identify a new lever for improvement; a null result would efficiently rule out fusion as a factor, narrowing the search to RNA encoder choice (scgpt, scvi) or other dimensions. No other single experiment isolates as important an untested variable with as minimal confounding.

The current best (config_002: pca_n2000, vit_l, avgpool, weighted → 0.635) establishes that multiprofile + vit_l + avgpool + weighted is the strongest pipeline. The RNA encoder is the largest untested design axis in this strong multiprofile setting: scgpt showed a negative signal in singleprofile (0.427 vs 0.527), but that was a fundamentally weaker setting, and scvi_n200 is completely untested anywhere. Config_020 (scvi_n200, vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable swap against config_002, isolating the effect of a learned variational RNA encoder while holding image encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed. This maximally reduces uncertainty about whether a learned RNA representation can improve over PCA in the best multiprofile pipeline, which is the most important remaining design question under the limited budget.

The strongest finding is that scvi_n200 dramatically outperforms pca_n2000 (0.706 vs 0.635 in config_020 vs config_002, same image/aggregation/fusion). However, with pca_n2000, transformer aggregation was notably worse than avgpool (0.599 vs 0.635 in config_045 vs config_002). This raises the question: does the richer, more structured scvi_n200 representation benefit from attention-based (transformer) aggregation in a way that the flat pca_n2000 representation did not? Config_028 (scvi_n200, vit_l, transformer, weighted) is a clean single-variable change from the current best (config_020), isolating the aggregation effect. If transformer matches or exceeds avgpool with scvi_n200, it reveals an important interaction between representation quality and aggregation strategy; if it underperforms, it confirms avgpool as the robust choice and narrows the search space. This is the highest-information next step because it directly extends the most promising direction while resolving a key design uncertainty that could guide all subsequent experiments.

The current best (config_028, scvi_n200 + ViT + transformer + weighted, 0.725 acc) suggests scvi_n200 and multimodal fusion are both important, but we have never tested scvi_n200 with multiprofile in an RNA-only setting. The gap between config_007 (pca, RNA-only, singleprofile: 0.485) and config_020 (scvi, multimodal, multiprofile: 0.706) conflates three changes simultaneously (encoder, profile, modality). Config_032 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) cleanly isolates how much of the 0.706 performance comes from the RNA representation and multiprofile aggregation alone versus the image modality. If RNA-only scvi approaches ~0.65+, the image contribution is modest and future effort should focus on RNA representation; if it stays near ~0.50–0.55, the multimodal combination is genuinely additive and justifies further multimodal exploration. This is the highest-information experiment under the limited budget because it resolves a critical uncertainty that will determine whether to exploit the multimodal direction further or pivot toward simpler RNA-centric designs.
